title: Expose onboarding affinity, soft/hard limits, and cost hints in model exposure schema
creator: Ava Patel
description: Add a new, backwards-compatible exposure schema that surfaces runtime affinity hints, soft vs hard limits, and token-level cost estimates to enable smarter client-side routing and automated fallbacks. This ticket defines the API contract (fields, types, semantics) and implements the server-side publication of these fields during model onboarding. The goal is to give SDKs and platform components enough signal to make deterministic routing, batching and quantization choices without embedding product heuristics in the model catalog consumers.
acceptance_criteria: API v1.1 endpoint returns 'exposure' object for every onboarded model with documented fields: runtime_affinity, context_window, soft_limits, hard_limits, latency_profile_samples, cost_hint_microdollars_per_token, quantization_support, kv_cache_behavior, suggested_batch_size, fallback_variant_ids
Existing clients that ignore new fields continue to operate without change (backwards-compatible addition), documented in API changelog
Integration test that verifies SDK routing picks alternative variant when soft_limits exceeded and hard_limits enforced by runtime (simulated)
Contract tests (OpenAPI + JSON Schema) published in repo and validated in CI for both hosted and dedicated onboarding flow
Conformance test that validates cost_hint tolerances are present for all models in model-catalog >= runtime-1.20 release
technical_notes: Add /models/{model_id}/exposure (GET) which returns an exposure object; also include exposure in /models/{id} for single-call convenience
Define 'soft_limits' as advisory thresholds (tokens/sec, request_size_tokens) and 'hard_limits' as runtime-enforced values (max_context_tokens, max_concurrent_streams)
Introduce 'runtime_affinity' semantic: list of affinity tags (low_latency, cost_optimized, high_throughput) and a numeric 'affinity_score' 0-100 to express preference magnitude
cost_hint provided as integer microdollars_per_token to avoid float mismatches (clients can divide by 1_000_000 to get dollars/token)
latency_profile_samples: quantile map as list of strings (e.g., 'p50:12ms', 'p95:120ms') to preserve ordering and readability in schema-level flat types
kv_cache_behavior: enum ["read_only", "read_write", "no_cache"] plus 'recommended_eviction_seconds' as advisory TTL
suggested_batch_size: numeric advisory used by SDK batching layer; will be used by optimizer to recommend autoscaler settings for Dedicated pools
Add 'compatibility_matrix' as a list of model variant ids and supported API version tags (flat strings)
No auth model changes; endpoint uses existing model-catalog permission checks. Ensure internal catalog publish path enriches exposure document during onboarding pipelines.
decisions: Represent cost hints in microdollars_per_token (integer) to avoid floating point non-determinism across languages
Expose advisory vs enforced limits explicitly to help client-side fallbacks instead of changing runtime enforcement behavior
Bundle exposure object into model manifest v1.1 rather than creating a separate service to simplify onboarding flow and reduce cross-service coupling
Avoid including raw telemetry or proprietary benchmarking identifiers in exposure payload; keep it high-level and machine-actionable
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Publish exposure for 10% of new onboarded models in staging and validate SDK reads advisory fields (2-week canary)
Phase 2 (internal): Enable exposure for all onboarding in internal-prod and run contract tests against downstream SDKs and routing services (1 week)
Phase 3 (public): Gradual publish to hosted catalog and flag in release notes; coordinate with SDK teams to add optional parser updates
Fallback: If consumers observe regressions, allow toggling exposure publication via feature-flag at catalog-publish pipeline
migration_strategy: Additive - clients that don't parse new fields continue to work. SDKs will gradually adopt 'affinity_score' and cost_hint to change routing heuristics. For Dedicated customers, autoscaler recommendations will read suggested_batch_size but not enforce it until admin opt-in.
tests: contract: SDK parsing + routing decision tests
e2e: hosted catalog consumption + routing fallback simulation
notes_for_sdk: SDKs should ignore unknown exposure fields until they adopt the parser
Add parser helpers: Exposure.getAffinity(), Exposure.getCostPerTokenMicros(), Exposure.getAdvisoryLimits()
Provide opt-in flag in SDK (routing.useExposure = true) to allow gradual adoption
